groups_from: A protein's Gene Ontology terms are those InterPro maps to any of its signatures and, for a UniProtKB entry, those UniProt gives the entry; a gene model takes also the terms of the entries joined to it. With every broader term (by the ontology's kind-of and part-of links), the protein falls in the first district, in the order listed, one of whose terms it carries. A family's members are one kind of protein, so it stands in the district most of its classed members fall in; of equal counts, the first listed. A part of no_family is a looser grouping: it stands in a district only if more than half of all its members fall there. The choice of the districts' terms and their order is the viewer's.
family_from: A family is an InterPro entry of the type Family (InterPro 111.0). A protein is filed under the narrowest family among its signatures: one that is not a broader kind of another it carries, by InterPro's tree of entries. Where several unrelated families remain (221 proteins), it is the deepest in that tree, then the one fewest proteins of this catalogue are in, then the first by accession. A gene model's signatures are those on any of its predicted proteins, as the catalogue lists them.

family_notes.side: The side most of the family's members sit on; of equal counts, a membrane first.
family_notes.units: The inventory units whose candidate products, in the planarian atlas, are members of this family.
family_notes.where: The places in the cell that the same Gene Ontology terms name for at least half of the family's members that are given any: an annotation carried by signatures, not a prediction for these proteins. nucleus: nucleus (GO:0005634); mitochondrion: mitochondrion (GO:0005739); endoplasmic reticulum: endoplasmic reticulum (GO:0005783); Golgi apparatus: Golgi apparatus (GO:0005794); lysosome: lysosome (GO:0005764); peroxisome: peroxisome (GO:0005777); cilium: cilium (GO:0005929); cytoskeleton: cytoskeleton (GO:0005856); ribosome: ribosome (GO:0005840); cytosol: cytosol (GO:0005829); plasma membrane: plasma membrane (GO:0005886); extracellular: extracellular region (GO:0005576).

members_from.order: The table's lines are the members in order: the families as listed here, then the parts of no_family as listed; within each, the catalogue's order. A family's members are the lines whose 'under' is its id.
members_from.files: A file holds the members of consecutive families: a new file begins where the next family or part would take it past 2,000 members, so a family or a part is never split, and one larger than that has a file of its own. 'file' names the file and 'at' the first and one past the last of its members there.
members_from.label: A member's label is its name in predicted_proteins.tsv; where that is empty, the label of the part it is filed under.
members_from.step: python3 tools/build_planarian_atlas.py members --out DIR writes the files from the two tables.

side_notes.predicted: Gene models: TMHMM (membrane-spanning helices) and SignalP (signal peptides) as WormBase ParaSite ran them on each model's predicted proteins and gives them in its BioMart (release 19); the gene's longest predicted protein is read. One helix or more without a signal peptide, or two or more with one: in a membrane. A signal peptide and no helix: outside. Neither, on a model that begins with methionine: inside. A signal peptide with exactly one helix (604 models) is settled by this tool's own reading of the sequence, because TMHMM can take a signal peptide for a helix: a stretch of 19 residues of which 12 or more are hydrophobic (A, F, I, L, M, V, W) that starts at residue 36 or later puts it in a membrane; such a stretch only before that puts it outside. UniProtKB entries: the membrane-spanning segments and signal peptides that UniProt's automatic annotation gives the entry. Which membrane a protein spans is not predicted: the shelf stands for the cell's membranes together.
side_notes.by function: Taken from an annotation: for a UniProtKB entry with nothing predicted, the subcellular location UniProt's rules give it; for a protein whose beginning is missing and on which nothing was predicted, the place its Gene Ontology terms name, where that leaves no real doubt.
side_notes.stated: A reviewed UniProtKB entry states the location, by similarity to another species' protein.
side_notes.not known: Nothing was predicted and the protein's beginning is missing, so a signal peptide could be missing with it; or the two predictors cannot be told apart.
